reply_acts.author: claude-17
reply_acts.text: Gist: C-c ; works in your buffer now. Your claude-17 REPL runs on its own copy of the key map, made before these bindings existed, so binding the mode map didn't reach it. The fix also binds the keys in any open REPL buffer like that (commit 1ee5fea7), and I checked that in *claude-repl:claude-17* C-c ; and C-c x p now run the right commands. I agree about the ledger and am dropping it: the marks should feed Elephant-2000's records, not a new store.

reply_acts.author: claude-17
reply_acts.text: (why the key was missing) Every other Claude REPL buffer already had C-c ;. Yours didn't even have C-a, which the current mode map binds, so it was clearly running on an older map. Loading the file now binds the keys in such buffers too.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the menu, commit 73bb40f7) It's loaded in your running Emacs now. I tested it there: pressing s, then typing ":yes", gave "🈸:yes".
- **Keys:** the letters follow the intent names where they can: p propose, a approve, d disagree, s ask-action, c clarify, n constrain, z defer, ! report-problem, and "." for unresolved. The menu shows the whole list.
- **Problem fixed:** a hydra hint has to start with a newline, or it fails when shown with "Not enough arguments for format string".

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(session, not ping-pong) A reply to the turn before it is only the simplest case. A 🈸 from Tuesday can be settled by a commit on Wednesday, or dropped without anyone saying so. So I'd keep a ledger of open items:
- **Opened by:** an agent's ㊭ or 🈸, or yours.
- **Closed by:** a marked answer (🈸:yes), an approve or disagree that 象 reads, a commit that carries the turn's trailers, or a later 🈡 withdraw.
- **Still open at the end of a session:** the "no response" class the paper says is missing.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what the War Machine offers) As I understand it from what's recorded here, the War Machine counts progress against a fixed list. Each click must clear an unchecked checklist item. Open obligations go to the front of selection. A repair comes before the next click if that click would repeat the last failure. Its room for learning is choosing from patterns it already has, as you said, plus "mint missing fundamentals first" as a deliberate, rare step. The ledger can borrow the first two directly: items carried across turns, and open items surfacing before new ones.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (what dialogue could give back) The difference you point to is that dialogue mints items all the time. The idea we're discussing now wasn't in any mission file. So the ledger should flag any item whose text has no close match among mission files, earlier ledger items or patterns as "minted in session X, turn Y". Those flags would give the War Machine a supply of new candidate items, each traceable to the conversation that produced it, instead of minting being an exception it handles alone. Whether the flags are accurate enough to use would show in the first week of data. A simple text match will both miss rephrasings and over-flag.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (one decision) Shall I build the ledger v0 over this session and the last few days? Agent marks since 30 September and your turns as 象 reads them, with open, closed and minted counts, and a short list of minted items for you to judge by eye.
